rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so the baseline table was too conservative; this round raises SecurityGain and DiversityGain across all seven passes to push coverage over more of the 23 small functions (make_list, make_wanted, make_play are the main targets for FLA/SPLIT/BCF since their larger bodies give flattening and splitting room to obscure control flow cheaply per byte). SUB and ICALL get high weights because arithmetic substitution and indirect-call conversion add strong static-analysis friction at low size cost, which suits a 6KB text segment where size headroom is limited. RuntimeCost and SizeCost are kept moderate rather than low because chomp/queens are recursive search workloads where BCF/FLA overhead compounds in hot loops — capping these at 0.5-0.6 lets the selector apply heavy passes to cold functions while sparing the hottest recursion. CorrectnessRisk stays at or below 0.5 everywhere: the previous round showed the toolchain handles these passes on this program, but IGV's global-variable rewriting and FLA's restructuring still warrant mid-range risk weights so pathological functions fall back safely rather than forcing an ICE.
